dedupe_keys.name: mnms multimodal network modelling and simulation agent based mfd urban mobility simulator

description: MnMS (Multimodal Network Modelling and Simulation) is an agent-based dynamic traffic simulator for urban mobility at large urban scale. Travellers choose modes and routes among all options on the city transport network, including private cars, public transport and new services such as ride-hailing, ride-sharing and vehicle sharing, while vehicle motion follows regional multimodal macroscopic fundamental diagram (MFD) curves, so vehicles of one type share a speed within a region at a given time. This lets it address the operation, optimisation and regulation of new mobility services and multi-stakeholder policy design. It results from the ERC MAGnUM project at Université Gustave Eiffel, with on-demand mobility extensions from the DIT4TraM project. It is generic and applies to any city. The code is free on GitHub under the GNU Lesser General Public License version 3, and a Zenodo record archives a snapshot of the repository (commit accessed 29 July 2026) under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the regional MFD approach does not represent individual links in detail, and calibration needs city-specific MFD curves. MnMS supports agent-based simulation of multimodal networks, capacity planning of mobility services and optimisation of fleet operations. It complements MATSim and the other agent-based models catalogued here.
